source_text: «Ζῶν γὰρ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ, φησὶ, καὶ ἐνεργὴς, καὶ τομώτερος ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν μάχαιραν δίστομον, καὶ διικνούμενος ἄχρι μερισμοῦ ψυχῆς καὶ πνεύματος, ἁρμῶν τε καὶ μυελῶν, καὶ κριτικὸς ἐνθυμήσεων καὶ ἐννοιῶν καρδίας. Καὶ οὐκ ἔστι κτίσις ἀφανὴς ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, πάντα δὲ γυμνὰ καὶ τετραχηλισμένα τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ, πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος.» Ἀνακαίοντος δὲ τοῦ ἱερέως τὸ πῦρ, ἐπιτίθεται τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ τὰ διχοτομήματα, σὺν τῇ κεφαλῇ καὶ τοῖς ποσὶ, καὶ μέντοι καὶ ἐνδοσθίοις, ἐκνενιμμένοις ὕδασιν. Εὐώδη γὰρ ἅπαντα τὰ τῶν ἁγίων, οὐδὲν ἀπόβλητον παρὰ Θεῷ τῶν ἐκείνοις ἐνεῖναι πεπιστευμένων. Εἶεν δ' ἂν εἰς τύπον τὰ μὲν κρέα, τῆς οἱονεὶ παχυτέρας αὐτῶν καὶ ἐνσωμάτου ζωῆς· σεμνὴ γὰρ αὐτὴ καὶ πάναγνος· κεφαλὴ δὲ, νοῦ σημεῖον, λογισμῶν δὲ καὶ ἐπιθυμιῶν, τὰ ἐντόσθια· πόδες δὲ αὖ, πρακτικῆς καὶ τῆς ὡς ἐν ἔργοις πορείας αἴνιγμα λεπτόν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὡς δριμὺς ὁ λόγος! {ΚΥΡ.} Ἔχει δ' οὖν ὅμως τὸ ἀληθὲς, καίτοι διάττων ἡμῖν ὡς ἐν ὁμίχλῃ καὶ σκότῳ· βαθὺς γὰρ ὁ νόμος. «Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν προβάτων, φησὶ, τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἀπό τε τῶν ἀρνῶν καὶ τῶν ἐρίφων εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα· ἄρσεν ἄμωμον προσάξει αὐτὸ, καὶ ἐπιθήσει τὴν χεῖρα ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ σφάξουσιν αὐτὸ, ἐκ πλαγίων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου πρὸς βοῤῥᾶν, ἔναντι Κυρίου.» Μελίζεται δὲ καὶ αὐτὸ, ἐκνενιμμένων τῶν ἐντοσθίων κατὰ τὸν ἴσον τῷ μόσχῳ τρόπον. Ἀνακομίζεσθαι δὲ δεῖν ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον ἐθεσμοθέτει πάλιν· ὁ αὐτὸς δ' ἂν εἴη τῆς θεωρίας καὶ ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγος. Πλὴν ἔχει τι παρηλλαγμένον· ἐσφάζετο γὰρ ὁ ἀμνὸς ἐκ πλαγίων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου πρὸς βοῤῥᾶν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τίς οὖν ἄρα ἐστὶ καὶ ὁ τοῦδε λόγος; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἢ οὐκ οἶσθα, ὅτι νοτιωτέρα πώς ἐστι τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἡ γῇ, τὰ δέ γε πρὸς θάλασσαν τὴν βορειοτέραν αἱ ἀναρίθμητοι τῶν ἐθνῶν ἀγέλαι διεμοιρήσαντο, κατὰ χώρας καὶ πόλεις συνῳκισμέναι; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές. {ΚΥΡ.} Αἴνιγμα δὴ οὖν τοῦ καὶ αὐτὰς τὰς εἰς βοῤῥᾶν ἀγέλας, ἱερὰς ἔσεσθαι τῷ Θεῷ, τὸ ὡς ἐν μέρει τῷ βορειοτέρῳ καταθύεσθαι τὸν ἀμνόν. Τοῦτό τοι καὶ ὁ Σωτὴρ περὶ τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἀγέλης προανεφώνει λέγων· «Καὶ ἄλλα πρόβατα ἔχω, ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης, κἀκεῖνά με δεῖ ἀγαγεῖν, καὶ γενήσεται μία ποίμνη, εἷς ποιμήν.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνῆκα ὃ φής. {ΚΥΡ.} Ῥᾳθυμίας δὲ ἀμείνους καὶ ὄκνου παντὸς ἐπέκεινα τιθεὶς ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς τοὺς οἵπερ ἂν ἕλοιντο πληροῦν τὰ νενομισμένα, καταλεαίνει τρόπον τινὰ τῆς καρποφορίας τὴν ὁδὸν, καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἔτι προβάτου μείοσι τὰ τῆς θυσίας ἀποπεραίνεσθαι δεῖν ἐπιτάττει, λέγων· «Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν πετεινῶν κάρπωμα προσφέρῃ δῶρον τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ προσοίσει ἀπὸ τῶν τρυγόνων, ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν περιστερῶν τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσοίσει αὐτὸ ὁ ἱερεὺς πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καὶ ἀποκνίσει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπιθήσει ὁ ἱερεὺς ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καὶ στραγγιεῖ τὸ αἷμα πρὸς τὴν βάσιν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου. Καὶ
pass_a_gloss: [Cyril, continuing] For living (ζῶν) the word (λόγος) of God, he says, and active (ἐνεργής), and sharper (τομώτερος) beyond every two-mouthed sword (μάχαιρα δίστομος), and passing through (διικνέομαι) as far as division (μερισμός) of soul (ψυχή) and spirit (πνεῦμα), of joints (ἁρμός) and marrows (μυελός), and judge (κριτικός) of reflections (ἐνθύμησις) and thoughts (ἔννοια) of heart; and there is no creature (κτίσις) unseen (ἀφανής) before him, but all naked (γυμνός) and laid bare (τραχηλίζω, pf.) to his eyes, toward whom for us the account (λόγος) [Heb 4:12-13]. The priest kindling (ἀνακαίω) the fire, the halved pieces (διχοτόμημα) are put on the altar (θυσιαστήριον) with head and feet and also entrails (ἐνδόσθια), washed out (ἐκνίπτω) with waters [Lev 1:7-9]. For fragrant (εὐώδης) are all the things of the saints (ἅγιοι); nothing cast away (ἀπόβλητος) with God of the things believed (πιστεύω, pf. pass.) to be in them. As a type (τύπος): the flesh (κρέα) = their thicker, as it were, and embodied (ἐνσώματος) life, for it is honorable (σεμνός) and all-pure (πάναγνος); the head = sign (σημεῖον) of mind (νοῦς); the entrails = of reasonings (λογισμοί) and desires (ἐπιθυμίαι); the feet = a fine riddle (αἴνιγμα λεπτόν) of the practical [life] (πρακτική) and of walking (πορεία) as in works (ἔργα). PALL.: How sharp/keen (δριμύς) the account! CYR.: Yet it has the truth, although darting (διάττω) for us as in mist (ὁμίχλη) and darkness; for deep (βαθύς) the law. If from the sheep (πρόβατα) his gift (δῶρον) to the Lord, from lambs (ἀρνός) and kids (ἔριφος) for a whole burnt offering (ὁλοκαύτωμα), he will bring a male (ἄρσεν) unblemished (ἄμωμος), and will put his hand on its head, and they will slaughter (σφάζω) it at the sides of the altar toward the north (βορρᾶς), before the Lord [Lev 1:10-11 LXX]. It too is cut limb by limb (μελίζω), the entrails washed, in the same way as the calf (μόσχος); he ordained (θεσμοθετέω) again it must be carried up (ἀνακομίζω) to the altar [Lev 1:12-13]; the same account of the contemplation (θεωρία) here too. Except it has something altered (παραλλάσσω): the lamb (ἀμνός) was slaughtered at the side of the altar toward the north. PALL.: What then is the account of this? CYR.: Or do you not know that the land of the Jews is somewhat more southern (νοτιώτερος), while the parts toward the more northern (βορειότερος) sea the countless herds (ἀγέλαι) of the nations (ἔθνη) divided among themselves (διαμοιράομαι), settled together (συνοικίζω) by countries and cities? PALL.: True. CYR.: A riddle then of the herds toward the north also being holy (ἱερός) to God: the lamb being sacrificed (καταθύω) as in the more northern part. This the Savior (Σωτήρ) also proclaimed beforehand (προαναφωνέω) about the herd from the nations: And other sheep I have which are not of this fold (αὐλή); those too I must bring, and there will be one flock (ποίμνη), one shepherd (ποιμήν) [John 10:16]. PALL.: I understood what you say. CYR.: Placing better than sloth (ῥᾳθυμία) and beyond all hesitation (ὄκνος) those who would choose to fulfill the things prescribed (τὰ νενομισμένα), the God of all smooths (καταλεαίνω) in a way the road of fruit-bearing/offering (καρποφορία), and orders (ἐπιτάσσω) that the things of the sacrifice must be completed (ἀποπεραίνω) even in things smaller than a sheep, saying: If from the birds (πετεινά) he brings a burnt offering (κάρπωμα) as gift to the Lord, he will bring from the turtledoves (τρυγών) or from the doves (περιστερά) his gift; and the priest will bring it to the altar, and will wring off (ἀποκνίζω) its head, and the priest will put it on the altar, and will drain out (στραγγίζω) the blood at the base (βάσις) of the altar. And [continues in section 6] [Lev 1:14-15].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …For ‘the word of God is living,’ he says, ‘and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart. And no creature is hidden before him, but all things are naked and laid bare to his eyes, to whom we must give account’ (Hebrews 4:12–13). As the priest kindles the fire, the divided pieces are laid on the altar, with the head and the feet, and the entrails too, washed with water (Leviticus 1:7–9). For everything that belongs to the saints is fragrant, and nothing that is believed to be in them is rejected by God. The flesh would be a type of their life in the body, the coarser life, so to speak; for it is honorable and wholly pure. The head is a sign of the mind; the entrails stand for thoughts and desires; and the feet, in turn, are a subtle figure of the active life and of our walk, as it were, in deeds.
Palladius: How subtle the argument is!

Cyril: Even so, it holds the truth, though it flashes past us as if through mist and darkness; for the law is deep. ‘If his gift to the Lord,’ it says, ‘is from the flock, from the lambs or from the kids, for a whole burnt offering, he shall bring a male without blemish, and he shall lay his hand on its head, and they shall slaughter it at the side of the altar toward the north, before the Lord’ (Leviticus 1:10–11). This victim too is cut into pieces, and its entrails are washed, in the same way as the calf; and again he laid down that it must be carried up onto the altar (Leviticus 1:12–13). The meaning of the spiritual reading would be the same in this case as well. Yet there is one difference: the lamb was slaughtered at the side of the altar toward the north.
Palladius: What, then, is the meaning of this?

Cyril: Do you not know that the land of the Jews lies somewhat to the south, while the countless flocks of the nations have divided among themselves the regions toward the northern sea, settled in countries and cities?

Cyril: The sacrifice of the lamb in the more northern part, as it were, is therefore a figure showing that the flocks toward the north will also be holy to God. This is what the Savior too foretold about the flock from the nations, when he said: ‘And I have other sheep that are not of this fold; I must bring them also, and there will be one flock, one shepherd’ (John 10:16).
Palladius: I understand what you mean.

Cyril: The God of all sets those who choose to fulfill what the law prescribes above sloth and beyond all reluctance: he in a way smooths the road of offering, and directs that the sacrifice be completed even with creatures smaller than a sheep, saying: ‘If he brings a gift to the Lord, a burnt offering from the birds, he shall bring his gift from the turtledoves or from the doves; and the priest shall bring it to the altar, and wring off its head, and the priest shall put it on the altar, and drain its blood at the base of the altar (Leviticus 1:14–15).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

Boundary in: section 5 opens inside Cyril’s turn; section 4 ends with the claim that the cutting into pieces shows God’s word reaching ‘joints and marrow’, so the Hebrews quotation is introduced by γάρ (‘For’) and the section starts ‘Cyril: …For’. Boundary out: the quotation of Leviticus 1:14–17 is split; the source section ends with the single word Καὶ, which opens Leviticus 1:16 (‘and he shall remove the crop’). That ‘and’ is rendered at the start of section 6, not here, so section 5 ends at ‘base of the altar (Leviticus 1:14–15).’ The opening quotation mark of the Leviticus quotation is closed in section 6. Hebrews 4:13 πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος rendered ‘to whom we must give account’ (could also be ‘with whom we have to do’). Leviticus 1:7–9 is a paraphrase, not a quotation (LXX: the sons of Aaron put fire on the altar, lay the pieces, head and fat, wash the entrails and feet). Leviticus 1:10–11 follows the LXX, which adds ‘and he shall lay his hand on its head’ in v. 10 (not in the Hebrew of v. 10). Leviticus 1:12–13 is paraphrase (cut into pieces, wash entrails, carry all to the altar). Palladius’ Ὡς δριμὺς ὁ λόγος: δριμύς means sharp or keen; Cyril’s reply (‘it flashes past us as if through mist’) shows Palladius means the reading is subtle and hard to grasp, so ‘How subtle the argument is!’. θεωρία rendered ‘spiritual reading’ (Cyril’s term for the figurative sense). ἀγέλαι (herds) rendered ‘flocks’ to keep the sheep image that leads into John 10:16. πρὸς θάλασσαν τὴν βορειοτέραν literally ‘toward the more northern sea’; rendered ‘toward the northern sea’. LXX περιστερά in Leviticus 1:14 (English Bibles: ‘young pigeons’) is rendered ‘doves’ because section 6 reads the bird as ‘the gentlest dove’. κάρπωμα rendered ‘burnt offering’ (LXX equivalent of the whole offering here). No LXX Psalm renumbering needed in this section.
